newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Wednesday on a technical rebound after heavy losses over the past few days, traders said.
The strong performance of the domestic A share markets also helped support the short-term contracts, they said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded three-day contract rose to 5.20 percent from 2.50 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell slightly to 1.69 million lots from 1.72 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said some institutions, including securities houses, were seen borrowing heavily, especially in early-maturing contracts.
But some long-term contracts, such as the 28-day contract which had risen on Tuesday, saw price corrections, they said.
Rates were expected to rise further if A share markets continued their strong run, but upward potential would be limited by a comparatively ample supply of funds, traders said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended up across the board on Wednesday because of the high yield rates of many contracts compared with bank deposit rates, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 112.61 yuan from 112.50 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 901,336 lots from 1.27 million lots.
"Some institutions have been investing in spot treasury bills, boosting both prices and volumes," one trader said.
Traders said they expected the incremental rises to slow down towards the end of the week, after solid gains in the past two days.
